code:
With a key:
  partition = hash(key) % numPartitions
  -> same key ALWAYS lands on the same partition (ordering)

Without a key (key = null):
  Kafka spreads round-robin across partitions
  -> even load, no per-value ordering guarantee
caption: Keying trades even load for guaranteed per-key order.

code:
Too FEW partitions:                Too MANY partitions:
- max parallel consumers            - more open file handles
  = partition count                 - slower leader elections
- extras just idle                  - more replication traffic
caption: Partition count directly bounds parallelism, in both directions.

code:
BAD key: "country"
  -> 90% of traffic from one country
  -> that one partition takes 90% of the load

BETTER key: "customer_id"
  -> high-cardinality, spreads evenly
caption: A hot partition looks like a slow consumer, not an error.
